3_architectural_issues.description: Violations of conventions from open-sse/AGENTS.md (DRY, config-driven, no hardcode)

issues.description: The SPECIAL_ADAPTERS object has providers hardcoded as string keys ("google-tts", "edge-tts", "local-device", "elevenlabs", "openai", "openrouter", "gemini", "xiaomi-mimo", "selfhosted-tts"). This violates the config-driven convention - new adapter providers require code changes rather than config updates.
issues.conventionViolation: Config-driven: NEVER hardcode values, models, or block/role strings — use config/ + schema/ constants. (open-sse/AGENTS.md line 11, 24)
issues.fix: Move adapter registry to config-driven approach where providers declare their TTS support in their registry entry, or use a naming convention that auto-maps provider IDs to adapter modules.
issues.evidence: synthesizeViaConfig() in the same file already demonstrates the config-driven pattern by reading AI_PROVIDERS[provider]?.ttsConfig from the provider registry.

issues.location: tests/vitest.config.js and multiple test files using @/... imports
issues.description: Test files use @/... aliases (e.g., '@/app/api/providers/route.js', '@/models/index.js', '@/lib/dataDir.js', '@/lib/db/driver.js') that don't resolve properly when running vitest from certain directories. The vitest config alias {find: /^@\//, replacement: resolve(__dirname, "../src") + "/"} works in some contexts but fails in others.
issues.conventionViolation: DRY: Test imports should resolve consistently without requiring relative path updates when directory structure changes.

fixOptions: Change @/... imports to relative paths (e.g., ../../../src/app/api/providers/route.js) - most reliable, works regardless of vitest config
Use absolute path for @/ alias: {find: /^@\//, replacement: resolve(__dirname, "../../src") + "/"} and ensure __dirname is correct
Create vitest config at project root that overrides tests config

issues.evidence: FIX_VITEST_ALIASES.md documents the issue completely; FIX_PLAN.md Priority 2 addresses this.

issues.category: Dynamic import inside function for config
issues.description: synthesizeViaConfig() uses a dynamic import() inside the function body to get AI_PROVIDERS. While this works, it's inconsistent with the pattern used elsewhere where AI_PROVIDERS is imported at the top level. The dynamic import creates an additional async boundary and may cause issues with module caching.
issues.conventionViolation: Config-driven: Values should be resolved from config at module load time, not runtime via dynamic import.
issues.fix: Move the AI_PROVIDERS import to module level or pass it as a parameter to synthesizeViaConfig.

issues.category: Font preconnect defined but not used in layout
issues.description: RESOLVED. The fontPreconnect constant and the viewport.fontPreconnect entry were defined but never produced a <link rel="preconnect"> in the HTML head. The attempt that did exist injected the <link> inside a <script> element, whose body is not valid script content, so the browser parsed it as script source and the preconnect never happened.
issues.conventionViolation: DRY: Defining a constant and not using it wastes developer time and creates false expectations. The web-performance-analysis.md explicitly recommends adding preconnect (Phase 5, High Impact/Low Effort).
issues.fix: DONE. next/font's Inter() already emits the preconnect to fonts.gstatic.com itself, so the dead constant, the dead viewport entry and the invalid inline <script> were removed. No manual <link> is needed.

issues.description: The font loading script has a 1-second timeout before forcing 'fonts-loaded' class. While 1s is better than the typical 3s, it could be further reduced or made configurable based on connection quality.
issues.conventionViolation: Performance: Hardcoded timeout without adaptive behavior.
issues.fix: Make the timeout configurable via env var or reduce further with critical font preload.

issues.category: handleTtsCore has adapter logic that should be config-driven
issues.description: The handleTtsCore function has a long list of special-cased adapter providers (lines 57-64). While some adaptation logic is inherently provider-specific, the pattern of checking for and dispatching to adapters could be more systematically configured rather than hardcoded in a switch-like object.
issues.conventionViolation: The system claims to be config-driven but has significant hardcoded dispatch logic in handleTtsCore.
issues.fix: Move adapter registry to provider registry entries with a 'ttsAdapter' field, or use a naming convention convention (e.g., provider "openai" auto-maps to openai.js adapter).

4_architectural_decision_records.description: ADRs for the four specified issues

adr1_tts_core_handler_pattern.title: TTS Core Handler: Adapter Pattern vs Config-Driven Pattern
adr1_tts_core_handler_pattern.context: The TTS handling in open-sse has two coexisting patterns: (1) SPECIAL_ADAPTERS object with hardcoded provider→adapter mappings in ttsProviders/index.js, and (2) synthesizeViaConfig() that is config-driven, reading AI_PROVIDERS[provider]?.ttsConfig and using FORMAT_HANDLERS. The adapter pattern works for known providers but violates the config-driven convention when new providers need code changes.
adr1_tts_core_handler_pattern.decision: Adopt a hybrid approach: Keep the adapter pattern for providers with significantly different API shapes (google-tts, edge-tts, local-device, elevenlabs, openai, openrouter, gemini, xiaomi-mimo, selfhosted-tts) but move the adapter registry to be populated from the provider registry entries. Each provider registry entry will have an optional 'ttsAdapter' field. For providers without a ttsAdapter field, fall through to the config-driven synthesizeViaConfig path. This preserves the performance of direct adapter calls while making the system extensible without code changes.

consequences.easier: New TTS providers can be added by updating the registry entry without modifying ttsProviders/index.js or handleTtsCore.js
consequences.harder: Initial setup requires updating the registry schema and ensuring all existing providers have correct ttsAdapter field values
consequences.tradeoff: Slightly more complex initial configuration but significantly easier long-term maintenance

adr2_vitest_alias_resolution.title: Vitest Import Alias Resolution Fix
adr2_vitest_alias_resolution.context: Test files across the codebase use @/... subpath aliases (e.g., '@/app/api/providers/route.js', '@/models/index.js', '@/lib/dataDir.js', '@/lib/db/driver.js') that fail to resolve consistently when running vitest from different directories. The vitest config in tests/vitest.config.js has alias {find: /^@\//, replacement: resolve(__dirname, "../src") + "/"} but this doesn't work reliably due to __dirname resolution issues and vitest configuration loading order.
adr2_vitest_alias_resolution.decision:
Apply Fix Option 1 from FIX_VITEST_ALIASES.md: Update all test file imports from @/... to relative paths. Specifically:
- tests/unit/bedrock-provider-api-secrets.test.js: @/app/api/providers/route.js → ../../../src/app/api/providers/route.js
- tests/unit/bedrock-provider-api-secrets.test.js: @/app/api/providers/[id]/route.js → ../../../src/app/api/providers/[id]/route.js
- tests/unit/bedrock-provider-api-secrets.test.js: @/models/index.js → ../../../src/models/index.js
- tests/unit/force-stream-config.test.js: @/lib/dataDir.js → ../../../src/lib/dataDir.js
- tests/unit/db-migration-chain.test.js: @/lib/db/driver.js → ../../../src/lib/db/driver.js

Rationale: This is the most reliable fix that works regardless of vitest configuration quirks or working directory. The test files are permanently in tests/unit/, so relative paths are predictable and stable.

consequences.easier: Imports will always resolve correctly; no dependency on vitest config __dirname resolution; works in any CI environment
consequences.harder: Requires updating import paths in 5 test files; relative paths are longer to type and more fragile to directory moves (mitigated by keeping tests in stable location)
consequences.tradeoff: One-time effort to update imports vs. ongoing vitest config maintenance

adr3_web_performance_fixes.title: Web Performance Fixes: Font Preconnect and Timeout Reduction
adr3_web_performance_fixes.context: The web-performance-analysis.md identified several high-impact, low-effort performance improvements. Two were flagged as not yet implemented: (1) font preconnect not added to layout head, and (2) font loading timeout at 1s could be optimized further. The layout.js defined a fontPreconnect constant and a viewport.fontPreconnect property but never produced a <link rel="preconnect"> tag in the HTML head; the one attempt that did exist injected the <link> inside a <script> element, whose body is not valid script content.
adr3_web_performance_fixes.decision:
IMPLEMENTED AS REVISED. The font preconnect is emitted by next/font's Inter() itself, so no manual <link> is needed: the dead constant, the dead viewport entry and the invalid inline <script> were removed rather than adding a second, redundant preconnect. The font loading timeout was reduced from 1000ms to 500ms in the inline script.

Additionally, verify Tailwind v4 purge configuration by running build and checking .next/ for unused class removal (estimated 50-100KB CSS reduction).

consequences.easier: Measurable performance improvements with minimal code changes (5 min each); improves Core Web Vitals ratings; no user-facing behavior changes
consequences.harder: Need to rebuild and verify no regressions; preconnect may have limited benefit if fonts are already cached by returning visitors
consequences.tradeoff: Small code changes for measurable performance gain; preconnect has diminishing returns for cached fonts

adr4_drift_prevention_framework.title: Drift Prevention Framework Implementation
adr4_drift_prevention_framework.context:
The STATUS_UPDATE.md and FINAL_SUMMARY.md document a 4-point drift prevention checklist designed to prevent AI agent code drift categories: (1) import resolution test, (2) full test suite, (3) pattern logic verification, (4) diff review. The investigation revealed that without all 4 checks, regressions are systematic and cumulative; with all 4 checks, drift is detected within 1 change, not 50 changes later.

However, the checklist is not yet enforced in CI/CD. The codebase has existing drift issues: vitest alias resolution failures, hardcoded values that violate config-driven conventions, and test expectations that don't match actual behavior.
adr4_drift_prevention_framework.decision:
Enforce the 4-point drift prevention checklist in CI/CD:

1. Import Resolution Test: Every PR must pass a test that validates all @/ and open-sse/ aliases resolve correctly. Run vitest with --resolveAliases and fail if any unresolved aliases exist.

2. Full Test Suite: Run the complete test suite (including open-sse provider tests) as part of CI. Currently some tests fail due to API key availability, but the suite structure exists.

3. Pattern Logic Verification: For any change to open-sse/providers/capabilities.js or pattern-matching logic, run the combo-caps-resolver.test.js and ensure expectations match actual behavior (or update expectations with proper rationale).

4. Diff Review: Mandatory diff review for all changes to open-sse/AGENTS.md conventions (config-driven, DRY, no hardcode). Use automated lint rules to flag hardcoded strings, missing config references, and pattern matching issues.

Additionally, create an automated drift detection job that compares baseline import graphs and pattern-matching outputs against current state on each commit.

The 4-point checklist should be added to GitHub Actions workflow (referenced in STATUS_UPDATE.md line 183: "Create drift prevention CI check").

consequences.easier: Drift detected immediately within a single change rather than accumulating over 50+ changes; clearer ownership of convention violations; faster onboarding for new AI agents
consequences.harder: Initial setup cost to add 4 CI checks and drift detection baseline; requires consistent enforcement to be effective; may slow down PR merge times initially
consequences.tradeoff: Upfront investment in CI infrastructure pays off by preventing systematic regressions; the 4 checks create a safety net that makes experimentation safer
